newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Foreign firms eye stake in SAfrica airport concern.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms eye stake in SAfrica airport concern.

text.p: A number of international concerns are interested in acquiring a minority stake, probably 49 percent, in South Africa's Airports Company which has been earmarked for partial privatisation, local media said on Tuesday.

Business Day said companies which have expressed interest include Lockheed Martin AGI, Soros Investments, BAA Plc, Schiphol Amsterdam, Daimler-Benz AG, the Malaysian Aiports Authority, Vienna Airport, Singapore Airport and Challenger Group.
Airports Company managing director Dirk Ackerman told state television that the operator of South Africa's main airports aimed to clinch a deal with a strategic equity partner by early next year.
"We hope to have that in place by the end of the calendar year or at the latest by the end of the financial year in March," he said.
Transport Minister Mac Maharaj believes the government could expect to receive around 1.2 billion rand for the sale of a 49 at about 2.5 billion rand.

The government has a 1.2 billion rand plan to transform the major airports at Johannesburg, Cape Town and Durban over the next five years, including new terminals at Johannesburg International. But the 1.2 billion suggested by government is significantly less than the 2.2 billion the Airports Company estimates is needed over the next five to six years. It hopes for further funds from a foreign partner.
